desks.Dividends: Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7%) and its 24th consecutive annual increase, payable Dec 10. Apple went ex-dividend Thu Nov 12 at $0.27, unchanged, payable Nov 16. Nvidia has not yet declared its fourth-quarter dividend; a December ex-date is plausible from cadence but UNVERIFIED. SPY and QQQ December ex-dates are unconfirmed. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus of $2.49 EPS and about $109 billion in revenue against company guidance of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. Options imply a move of about 8.5% (Nov 18 straddle), above the 4.78% average earnings-day move over the last four prints. It is the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang resigned Nov 11; the board has not given a reason. Premium into a binary event is to be avoided.
desks.Futures: The EIA weekly petroleum report, released Thu Nov 12 after a Veterans Day delay, showed commercial crude up 4.657 million barrels to 414.4 million, against a draw expected; gasoline rose 1.8 million and distillate 4.1 million. Brent still settled up 3.3% at $95.82 and WTI up 2.6% at $88.74 after the Houthis claimed attacks on the Saudi East-West Pipeline and Yanbu; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed any damage, so the move is risk premium, not confirmed supply loss. The November WASDE landed Tue Nov 10: corn ending stocks cut 91 million bushels, soybeans down 15 million; the corn and soybean pops faded the next day. OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
desks.Parity: No new parity-violation report or index-methodology change was published in the last 24 hours. The S&P growth/value methodology overhaul announced Oct 23 takes effect Dec 21; it changes growth/value classification, not S&P 500 membership, so there is no direct SPY composition change. No new published box-spread or put-call parity violation study was found.
desks.Premium: All six verdicts are WINDOW-CONTINGENT. The Nov 5 jump still drives 37-54% of each 20-day realized-variance window, so the gap between implied vol and trailing realized vol at 3 days to expiry on all six names is most plausibly the jump inflating realized, not cheap premium. Nvidia is the standout: at-the-money implied vol of 81.30% on the Nov 20 expiry, up 38.66 points over the Nov 16 expiry, because Nov 17 earnings sits inside the Nov 20 expiry — the elevation is the event being priced, and premium into it is to be avoided. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names: no free IV-history source is available.
desks.Quant lab: Seventeen new candidates were scored and added to the ledger (#268-284), four WATCH and thirteen ARCHIVE, with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. The top score, #269 (56), is TAPES, an error-scheduling method for diffusion samplers adjacent to the desk's IV-surface lane; #284 (54) finds IV-surface features lift HAR-RV R-squared in-sample. All claims are source-reported and UNVERIFIED; no code release exists for any WATCH candidate, so reproducibility is not established. Candidate #25 moved to v4 with an unresolved code-repository identity discrepancy.

headline: Daily research brief — Friday, November 13

items.detail: Nvidia reports Tue Nov 17 after close, the only watchlist earnings in the window. Consensus is $2.49 EPS and about $109 billion in revenue against company guidance of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. Options imply a move of about 8.5% (Nov 18 straddle), above the 4.78% average earnings-day move over the last four prints, though the Aug print rose 8.74%, so an 8-9% day is inside the recent range. It is the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang resigned Nov 11 (8-K filed Nov 12); the Q4 guide is likely to matter more than the Q3 print. The Nov 18 call quotes were crossed at pull time, so treat the 8.5% as approximate.
items.title: Nvidia's Nov 17 print is the only earnings event in the window, with an 8.5% move implied

items.detail: At-the-money implied vol on the Nov 20 expiry is 81.30%, up 38.66 points over the Nov 16 expiry, because Nov 17 earnings sits inside the Nov 20 expiry and not the Nov 16 expiry. That is the event being priced, not rich premium in the value sense, and premium into a binary event is to be avoided. Outside Nvidia, near-term implied vol is low versus a crash-polluted realized window, and the one genuinely elevated print is an earnings hump.
items.title: Nvidia premium into Nov 17 is the standing avoid — the market has already marked it up

items.detail: The Nov 5 crash day still drives 37-54% of each name's 20-day realized variance, above the 30% threshold, so no clean cheap-or-rich premium verdict is supportable on any name today. At 3 days to expiry, implied vol sits below trailing realized vol on all six names, but that gap is inflated by the crash day in realized. The window un-contaminates only after about Nov 25, when the Nov 5 day exits the 20-day window. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names: no free IV-history source is available.
items.title: Every IV-versus-realized verdict is window-contingent — no clean premium call on any name

items.detail: FRED as of Nov 12: the effective federal funds rate is 3.88%, the 2-year Treasury 4.86% (up 13 basis points from Nov 10), and the 10-year 5.10% (up 12 basis points), putting the 2s10s slope at +24 basis points. The Dec 9 call is unchanged: a 25 basis point hike, 5 HIKE / 1 CUT / 4 NEUTRAL across the ten core indicators, with Kalshi pricing the 25 basis point outcome at $0.87 and the larger-hike tail at $0.12. At assumed perpetual growth of 3.00%, the Gordon multiple falls to 47.62x from 50.51x, down 5.71%; re-anchor the discount rate to 5.10%.
